{"id": "7:195/q25", "question": "How are the final yāʾs of كِيدُونِ and تُنظِرُونِ read?", "turns_on": "The reader and transmission, pause versus continuation, and rhyme-like deletion versus original form.", "positions": [{"id": "7:195/q25/p1", "position": "Many readers omit the first-person yāʾ of kaydūn in continuation and pause.", "reasons": "Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī are repeatedly listed; Warsh, Qālūn, and al-Musayyibī also omit it. Ibn Dhakwān's written and memorized reports differ. The nūn's kasra implies the pronoun; al-Samīn compares 77:39."}, {"id": "7:195/q25/p2", "position": "Abū ʿAmr and some others retain kaydūnī's yāʾ in continuation only.", "reasons": "Nāfiʿ in named transmissions, Abū Jaʿfar, and al-Dājūnī from Hishām are also reported. Al-Samīn corrects Abū Ḥayyān: Abū ʿAmr always drops it at pause. Qiraat-ER notes full continuous yāʾ against a pausal sukūn."}, {"id": "7:195/q25/p3", "position": "Hishām and Yaʿqūb are reported retaining kaydūnī's yāʾ in both contexts.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Jazarī prefers the majority Hishām report over a continuation-only report, instructing that al-Taysīr be read accordingly. Al-Ḥulwānī, Ibn Suwār, Ibn Fāris, and Qunbul through Ibn Shanabūdh are also reported; 11:55 retains yāʾ universally."}, {"id": "7:195/q25/p4", "position": "Most omit the yāʾ of tunẓirūn; Yaʿqūb retains it in continuation and pause.", "reasons": "Al-Jishumī, Ṭabrisī, Ibn al-Jawzī, Ibn al-Jazarī, and Ibn ʿĀshūr give Yaʿqūb's form. Al-Ajhūrī's contrary claim of universal omission is reported by al-Ālūsī. Qiraat-ER says the full yāʾ makes the pronoun explicit."}, {"id": "7:195/q25/p5", "position": "Deletion follows verse-end rhyme practice; retention follows the underlying form.", "reasons": "Al-Fārisī, al-Wāḥidī, Abū ʿAlī, Ṭabrisī, and Rāzī cite poetry, including al-Aʿshā's an yaʾtiyan and yalmis al-aḥlās. Al-Jishumī adds eased pronunciation; Ibn ʿĀshūr calls deletion eloquent. Samarrai contrasts concise and extended contexts, excepting verse endings and vocatives."}]}
{"id": "7:195/q26", "question": "Why is the yāʾ shorter here than in Hūd?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:195/q26/p1", "position": "Al-Aʿrāf's concise challenge suits short forms; Hūd's longer confrontation suits pronounced yāʾ.", "reasons": "Samarrai says Hūd is more intense and repeats first-person yāʾ; al-Aʿrāf uses it once in 7:196. He notes the general link between written yāʾ and expanded context, with verse-end and vocative exceptions."}, {"id": "7:195/q26/p2", "position": "Al-Aʿrāf stresses swift punishment, while Hūd has fuller accounts and respite.", "reasons": "Samarrai compares ʿĀd (7:72; 11:58–60), Ṣāliḥ (7:78; 11:66–67), and Noah (7:63–64; 11:32–33). Al-Aʿrāf places thumma before fa, like 7:95's respite then sudden seizure; Hūd reverses."}]}
{"id": "7:195/q27", "question": "How do ثُمَّ and فَ order the challenge?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:195/q27/p1", "position": "Thumma introduces plotting after summoning; fa gives the immediate no-respite command.", "reasons": "Samarrai contrasts Hūd's reversed order and relates fa to immediacy and thumma to interval; 7:95 offers a parallel. Elsewhere he notes thumma works in commands and reports and can order statements without later events, citing 44:48, 2:199, 10:46, 11:3, 11:52, and poetry."}]}
{"id": "7:195/q28", "question": "What prophetic challenges echo this verse?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:195/q28/p1", "position": "Hūd and Noah issue analogous challenges; God's challenge to deniers also echoes the scheme motif.", "reasons": "Al-Zamakhsharī and Abū Ḥayyān cite Hūd's response after claims that gods harmed him (11:54–55). The Study Quran adds Noah (10:71), 77:39, 35:44, and 7:182–183. Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes other prophets' challenges."}]}
{"id": "7:195/q29", "question": "What inward response follows recognizing the true protector?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:195/q29/p1", "position": "Reliance on God cuts hope in creatures and brings contentment with His care.", "reasons": "Al-Qushayrī says God alone guides, answers, meets need, and controls harm; when He withholds, contentment in the innermost self exceeds gifts to the heart. Al-Bursawī's Persian couplet voices fearlessness even against both worlds."}, {"id": "7:195/q29/p2", "position": "Inner sight surpasses mere physical looking.", "reasons": "Al-Qushayrī says idolaters' hearts were veiled despite seeing idols; spiritual sight of masters is an unveiling proportionate to reverence and faith."}, {"id": "7:195/q29/p3", "position": "Faith and hypocrisy can coexist, with the prevailing element determining a heart's fate.", "reasons": "Salman distinguishes covered, inverted, mixed, and bare hearts; the believer's heart holds a lamp. Faith is a watered plant, hypocrisy a pus-fed sore; whichever prevails consumes its host."}]}
{"id": "7:195/q30", "question": "What associated Arabic examples illuminate ellipsis?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:195/q30/p1", "position": "Arabic may leave an alternative, verb, noun, or participle unspoken when context supplies it.", "reasons": "Ibn Qutayba cites an unnamed poet omitting the second alternative after ahum hamamtuhu; Abū Dhuʾayb implies am ghayy; another line implies muqbilan after raʾatnī bi-ḥablayhā; Dhū al-Rumma implies aqbala before al-layl; the Umm Salim line implies sabīl; al-Namir's aynamā implies dhahab. Samarrai describes contextual omissions of letters, verbs, nouns, and parallel features."}]}
{"id": "7:195/q31", "question": "What associated examples illustrate rhetorical implication and poetic comparison?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:195/q31/p1", "position": "Context selects one implication where a noun form can suggest several.", "reasons": "Al-Jurjānī explains indefinite shar in shar aharra dhā nāb; arajul atāka am imraʾah asks gender, whereas arajul atāka am rajulān asks number."}, {"id": "7:195/q31/p2", "position": "Conventional signs and lexical use govern a poem's meaning.", "reasons": "Al-Jurjānī says tears signify grief and rejects reading dry eyes as reunion's joy: jumūd is a defect, like a rainless year or milkless camel."}, {"id": "7:195/q31/p3", "position": "Indefiniteness may restrict a benefit to a future part rather than every case.", "reasons": "Al-Jurjānī says desire targets what is absent; 2:179's ḥayāh and 16:69's healing name partial benefits. Retribution saves the intended victim rather than the deterred murderer."}, {"id": "7:195/q31/p4", "position": "Imitation and eloquence require purposeful arrangement of meanings, not recitation or meter alone.", "reasons": "Al-Jurjānī says repeating Imruʾ al-Qays makes no poet; a Qurʾanic match needs meanings requiring its sequence, and meter is not eloquence."}, {"id": "7:195/q31/p5", "position": "Poetic parallels compare distinct images and paradoxes.", "reasons": "Al-Jurjānī lists gifts across Najd and lowlands, enticement and refusal, desire versus glory, veiled sunlight, eyes wounding hearts, safety as disease, perfection hastening decline, fewer visits preserving love, modest benefaction, and calamity striking the best."}, {"id": "7:195/q31/p6", "position": "Denying a necessary concomitant can deny its subject.", "reasons": "Al-Burhān applies this to idols' eyes and ears. Ibn al-Munīr separately defends Jarīr's use of 'before' to negate evil, against al-Aṣmaʿī, Khalaf, and Ibn Rashīq, citing 18:109 and 13:2."}]}
{"id": "7:195/q32", "question": "What associated reports describe units and modes of revelation?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:195/q32/p1", "position": "Reports recommend learning five verses at a time and say Gabriel conveyed five.", "reasons": "Al-Suyūṭī cites Abū Saʿīd, ʿUmar, and Abū al-ʿĀliya. A weak ʿAlī report adds memory protection except al-Anʿām. If sound, the report describes memorization in groups, not an exclusive revelation pattern."}, {"id": "7:195/q32/p2", "position": "Revelation may mean manifested recitation or God's teaching Gabriel; delivery has two modes.", "reasons": "Al-Iṣfahānī says Sunnis agree divine speech is revealed but differ over meaning. The Prophet may rise toward angelic form or Gabriel descend in human form; the former is harder."}]}
{"id": "7:195/q33", "question": "What adjacent reading and grammar notes accompany this verse?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:195/q33/p1", "position": "A light negative inna reading makes ʿibād accusative, but its construction is disputed.", "reasons": "Al-Bayḍāwī reports it as like Ḥijāzī mā yet says it is unattested; al-Ālūsī says the reading reinforces idol incapacity and lack of likeness."}, {"id": "7:195/q33/p2", "position": "Other reading discussions mention ayh and extra yāʾ locations.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Jazarī introduces alif deletion in ayh and two distinctive Qunbul yāʾs before the excerpts end; al-Mubhij uniquely reports Abū Nashīt affirming a yāʾ against other transmitters, and eight extra yāʾs including thumma kaydūn are listed."}]}
{"id": "7:195/q34", "question": "How does the verse fit the sūra's closing warning?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:195/q34/p1", "position": "The final section renews warnings against denial of God's signs and idolatry.", "reasons": "The Study Quran describes the final section this way."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q01", "question": "Who are those with your Lord?", "turns_on": "Whether the phrase specifies angels, includes all spiritually near servants, or receives an inward reading.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q01/p1", "position": "The angels, sometimes specified as the angels of the highest assembly.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās and other exegetes are cited by al-Wāḥidī; al-Ṭabrisī cites al-Ḥasan. Al-Qurṭubī calls the identification unanimous; Ibn ʿĀshūr relates their model role to the Messenger's rank. Elmalılı cites 39:75."}, {"id": "7:206/q01/p2", "position": "All who are brought near to God, not angels alone.", "reasons": "Ṭabāṭabāʾī says remembrance lifts the veil of

absence although all things are otherwise equally related to God; limiting the phrase to angels would defeat the exhortation to human remembrance."}, {"id": "7:206/q01/p3", "position": "Prophets, messengers, and Imams.", "reasons": "Reported by Ṭabāṭabāʾī from Tafsīr al-Qummī."}, {"id": "7:206/q01/p4", "position": "Those annihilated in divine unity and abiding through God.", "reasons": "Al-Qāshānī describes steadfast spiritual subsistence; Najmiyya as transmitted by Bursevī describes effacement of actions, traits, and selves."}, {"id": "7:206/q01/p5", "position": "A metaphor for utter God-consciousness.", "reasons": "Asad's formulation."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q02", "question": "What does ʿind convey here?", "turns_on": "Whether nearness describes rank or favor, an honored place or mission, proximity to the Throne, or spatial proximity to God.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q02/p1", "position": "Figurative nearness in rank, honor, mercy, and favor, without spatial proximity.", "reasons": "Al-Zajjāj cites mercy and favor while God is in heaven and earth (6:3); al-Rāzī compares minister and doorkeeper and cites the divine report about broken hearts. Ibn ʿAṭiyya, al-Ṭabrisī, and others deny bodily location; al-Burhān cites 3:169. Al-Ṭabrisī says God transcends place."}, {"id": "7:206/q02/p2", "position": "An honorific association with their distinguished dwelling and the place where divine commands issue.", "reasons": "Al-Wāḥidī cites people of meaning; al-Rāzī describes the realm of lights, spirits, obedience, and blessings."}, {"id": "7:206/q02/p3", "position": "Their location is wholly governed by God's decree.", "reasons": "Al-Naḥḥās and al-Qurṭubī report a place where nothing occurs save His decree; al-Ṭabrisī likens their relation to soldiers under a prince's authority."}, {"id": "7:206/q02/p4", "position": "They are God's messengers to creation, as troops can be said to be with a distant ruler.", "reasons": "The analogy is reported by al-Naḥḥās, al-Wāḥidī, al-Rāzī, and al-Qurṭubī."}, {"id": "7:206/q02/p5", "position": "Near the Lord's Throne.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī reports this as another interpretation."}, {"id": "7:206/q02/p6", "position": "Physical proximity implying God occupies a place and direction.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī attributes this to anthropomorphists and rejects it by rational and transmitted proofs discussed under 7:54 and 10:3."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q03", "question": "What range of meaning does ʿind have in Arabic?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q03/p1", "position": "It primarily conveys nearness, literal or figurative, and context can make it mean before or behind.", "reasons": "Al-Burhān compares ladā and waraʾ and cites 18:79, 14:16, 2:91, and 59:14 for contextual direction."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q04", "question": "Why is the group described by a relative clause instead of named as angels?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q04/p1", "position": "The description signals their exalted station and urges people to emulate them.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr says the wording invites competition in their conduct."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q05", "question": "What does their lack of istikbār mean?", "turns_on": "Whether the absence of pride is explained as obedient humility or inward effacement of ego.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q05/p1", "position": "They do not act proudly or deem themselves too exalted for worship.", "reasons": "Al-Jishumī derives istikbār from the form istifʿāl, seeking greatness by rejecting truth. Abū Ḥayyān says pride imagines superiority and obstructs obedience; al-Biqāʿī says angels neither show nor seek pride despite purity and rank."}, {"id": "7:206/q05/p2", "position": "They have no ego veil or independent self-claim.", "reasons": "Al-Qāshānī speaks of witnessing differentiation in unity; Bursevī's Najmiyya account says effacing one's acts removes pride."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q06", "question": "What is their ʿibāda?", "turns_on": "Whether ʿibāda is general obedience and reverence or specifically prayer.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q06/p1", "position": "Obedient submission and humble reverence to God.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī identifies humility as worship; Ibn al-Jawzī reports obedience; al-Ālūsī and Bursevī stress doing what was commanded. Kuran Yolu defines worship as acknowledging Lordship and showing respect by specified acts."}, {"id": "7:206/q06/p2", "position": "Prayer with humility within it.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Jawzī reports this alternative."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q07", "question": "What does their tasbīḥ mean?", "turns_on": "Whether tasbīḥ is transcendence in thought and speech, a formula, prayer, or inward self-negation.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q07/p1", "position": "They declare God transcendent above evil, imperfection, and all unfitting attributes.", "reasons": "Al-Jishumī stresses inadmissible attributes; Ibn ʿĀshūr includes speech and belief; al-Biqāʿī links angelic purity to freedom from desire; Kuran Yolu adds exaltation."}, {"id": "7:206/q07/p2", "position": "They say Subḥān Allāh and remember God.", "reasons": "Al-Baghawī supplies the utterance; Ibn al-Jawzī reports it as a distinct gloss; Muqātil says remembrance."}, {"id": "7:206/q07/p3", "position": "Their glorification is prayer.", "reasons": "Ibn Abī Ḥātim reports this from al-Suddī."}, {"id": "7:206/q07/p4", "position": "It negates association by effacing selfhood.", "reasons": "Al-Qāshānī and al-Ālūsī's inward interpretation."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q08", "question": "What does the imperfect verb suggest about glorification?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q08/p1", "position": "Its action recurs and continues.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr notes renewed continuous praise; al-Sāmarrāʾī says tasbīḥ and istighfār commonly take a verb for renewed action, citing 62:1."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q09", "question": "What does their sujūd mean?", "turns_on": "Whether sujūd denotes the bodily act, prayer, humble submission, or inward self-effacement.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q09/p1", "position": "Actual prostration to God, including prostration in prayer.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabrisī attributes the prayer detail to al-Ḥasan; Kuran Yolu describes lowering the head to the ground before God alone."}, {"id": "7:206/q09/p2", "position": "Prayer.", "reasons": "Muqātil, Ibn al-Jawzī, and al-Qurṭubī use prayer as the gloss."}, {"id": "7:206/q09/p3", "position": "Humble submission, especially exclusive servitude to God.", "reasons": "Al-Naḥḥās contrasts sinners; al-Ṭabrisī gives humility among alternatives; al-Bayḍāwī, al-Biqāʿī, and al-Ālūsī stress worship without association."}, {"id": "7:206/q09/p4", "position": "Complete inward annihilation of selfhood.", "reasons": "Al-Qāshānī says God alone remains after creation perishes; al-Ālūsī repeats the inward reading."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q10", "question": "Why is lahu placed before yasjudūn?", "turns_on": "Whether fronting principally creates exclusivity or serves the surrounding verse endings.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q10/p1", "position": "To restrict prostration to God alone and censure those who worship others.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī notes the restriction; Abū Ḥayyān reports this view; Bursevī and Ibn ʿĀshūr say the fronting censures polytheists, and Ibn ʿĀshūr adds that the imperfect conveys continuity."}, {"id": "7:206/q10/p2", "position": "To make the clause fit the verse ending.", "reasons": "Abū Ḥayyān prefers this over restriction; al-Ṭībī also mentions the verse ending alongside the moral rationale."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q11", "question": "Why are glorification and prostration mentioned in that order?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q11/p1", "position": "Inward knowledge and purification of God precede bodily worship, which grows from them.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī identifies heart then body; Abū Ḥayyān says freedom from pride produces both, with prostration the servant's closest state. Al-Biqāʿī says speech and action both return to the heart and cites the saying on nearness in prostration."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q12", "question": "How can exclusive prostration to God fit the angels' prostration to Adam?", "turns_on": "Which angels were commanded to prostrate, or whether a particular command qualifies the verse's general wording.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q12/p1", "position": "Only earthly angels prostrated to Adam, not the great heavenly angels.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī cites al-Ghazālī and 15:30, 38:73."}, {"id": "7:206/q12/p2", "position": "The command concerning Adam is a particular exception to a general statement.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī reports that the particular prevails over the general, citing 15:30 and 38:73."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q13", "question": "Why are the angels' worship and humility cited here?", "turns_on": "Whether the emphasis falls on emulation and rebuke, misplaced hopes for intercession, or spiritual joining through remembrance.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q13/p1", "position": "Their greater rank and constant devotion urge humans to worship and rebuke arrogant unbelievers.", "reasons": "Muqātil contrasts Meccans; al-Māwardī, al-Wāḥidī, al-Rāzī, and Study Quran reason from more honored angels to humans. Al-Rāzī cites 19:31 and 15:99; al-Kashshāf stresses exclusive worship; Ibn ʿĀshūr calls rebuke of polytheists the primary hint and cites Ibn Dāra's poem for emulation. Kuran Yolu says worship lifts humans beyond animal limits."}, {"id": "7:206/q13/p2", "position": "Their own worship challenges idolaters' expectation of angelic intercession.", "reasons": "Iṣlāḥī says idolaters slight God and the Prophet while expecting angels to intercede; the angels themselves glorify and prostrate."}, {"id": "7:206/q13/p3", "position": "It calls the servant to join the company of those near God through remembrance.", "reasons": "Ṭabāṭabāʾī connects the verse to the previous command; Iṣlāḥī says earthly rememberers join the angelic assembly; Elmalılı says remembrance and prostration open the way from the Heights to Paradise."}]}

question": "Does citing angels as models establish that they outrank prophets or humans?", "turns_on": "Whether exhortation by an angelic model entails an absolute ranking.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q14/p1", "position": "Yes, since the Messenger is urged to worship by appeal to their worship.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī reports Abū Bakr al-Aṣamm's argument."}, {"id": "7:206/q14/p2", "position": "No; acquired human imitation of angelic traits can be more meritorious.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects the Muʿtazilite inference and says the human achievement is more remarkable."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q15", "question": "What incident is reported behind the verse?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q15/p1", "position": "Meccan unbelievers refused or questioned prostrating at the Prophet's command; the verse answered them with the angels' example.", "reasons": "Muqātil, al-Māwardī, Ibn al-Jawzī, and al-Kāshifī cite the objection in 25:60; al-Kāshifī says aversion increased."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q16", "question": "How does the verse connect to the preceding commands and the sūra's story?", "turns_on": "Whether the link is chiefly to nearby remembrance commands or to the sūra's opening narrative.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q16/p1", "position": "It explains and motivates the preceding commands to listen, remember, and supplicate by the angels' example.", "reasons": "Al-Jishumī cites 7:204; Ibn ʿĀshūr says emphatic in marks a rationale rather than doubt and links 7:203–204 to believers' prostration; Ṭabāṭabāʾī says remembrance brings one among the near; Iṣlāḥī reads the ending as help to persevere against objections."}, {"id": "7:206/q16/p2", "position": "The ending recalls the opening Adam story: angels prostrate humbly whereas Iblīs refused proudly.", "reasons": "Al-Biqāʿī also relates it to the opening command to follow the Qurʾan; al-Sāmarrāʾī traces pride and prostration across the sūra."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q17", "question": "What other Qurʾanic descriptions illuminate the angels here?", "turns_on": "Which parallel passage or report supplies the connection.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q17/p1", "position": "Other verses describe their continuous glorification, standing, and prostration.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī cites 37:165–166 and 39:75; Study Quran cites 13:13, 39:75, 42:5 and prostration at 16:49; the sky-groaning report has angels standing, bowing, and prostrating in every handspan."}, {"id": "7:206/q17/p2", "position": "It echoes 4:172, where Jesus and angels do not disdain God's service.", "reasons": "Study Quran identifies the parallel."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q18", "question": "What level of remembrance does this verse call for?", "turns_on": "Whether the emphasis is degree of continuity or inward as well as outward form.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q18/p1", "position": "Regular but intermittent remembrance below the angels' uninterrupted glorification.", "reasons": "Ṭabāṭabāʾī compares 21:19–20 and 41:38, where the near glorify without weariness."}, {"id": "7:206/q18/p2", "position": "Remembrance includes inward awareness as well as speech and bodily action.", "reasons": "Ṭabāṭabāʾī cites creation's glorification and prostration at 17:44, 55:6, 13:15."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q19", "question": "Why is this a place of recitation prostration?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q19/p1", "position": "Reciters prostrate here to imitate the angels and oppose unbelievers' refusal; it is the first such place in muṣḥaf order.", "reasons": "Al-Māwardī, Ibn Kathīr, and Ibn ʿĀshūr call it first. Al-Ṭabrisī reports consensus; Ibn Kathīr extends consensus to listeners. Ibn ʿĀshūr cites Ibn ʿAbbās that sajdah sites frustrate polytheists or emulate prophets, including David at 38:24 under 6:90. Bursevī adds remediation of deficiency as another general purpose."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q20", "question": "May one bow instead of prostrating at this marker?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q20/p1", "position": "Yes, either bowing or prostration is allowed.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports al-Nakhaʿī via al-Naqqāsh."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q21", "question": "How many recitation prostrations are counted in the Qurʾān?", "turns_on": "Which sites are included, especially the second al-Ḥajj prostration, Ṣād, al-Ḥijr, and the short sūras; al-Qurṭubī cites varying reports and disagreement over commands.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q21/p1", "position": "Fifteen, including two in al-Ḥajj and the short sūras.", "reasons": "Ibn Ḥabīb, a report from Ibn Wahb, and Isḥāq are cited; Study Quran says fifteen. The report to ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ gives fifteen but ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq doubts Ibn Munayn; ʿUqbah's report for two in al-Ḥajj contains very weak Ibn Lahīʿah. ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ reports that the Prophet taught him fifteen prostration sites, specifying three in al-Mufaṣṣal and two in al-Ḥajj."}, {"id": "7:206/q21/p2", "position": "Fourteen, counting Ṣād but omitting the second al-Ḥajj prostration.", "reasons": "Ibn Wahb and the Ḥanafīs; al-Qurṭubī prefers omitting second al-Ḥajj because its report is unsound. Abū Ḥayyān compares Abū Ḥanīfa's locations with al-Shāfiʿī's."}, {"id": "7:206/q21/p3", "position": "Fourteen, counting the second al-Ḥajj prostration but omitting Ṣād.", "reasons": "Al-Shāfiʿī's count; Abū Ḥayyān says the two fourteen-count positions differ in those locations."}, {"id": "7:206/q21/p4", "position": "Sixteen, adding al-Ḥijr 15:98.", "reasons": "Al-Qurṭubī and Abū Ḥayyān report the addition."}, {"id": "7:206/q21/p5", "position": "Eleven, omitting second al-Ḥajj and three in al-Mufaṣṣal.", "reasons": "The famous Mālikī count, also attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn ʿUmar; Abū al-Dardāʾ reports eleven with the Prophet and lists the sites. Abū al-Dardāʾ specifies the eleven places where he prostrated with the Prophet: al-Aʿrāf, al-Raʿd, al-Naḥl, Banī Isrāʾīl, Maryam, al-Ḥajj, al-Furqān, al-Naml, al-Sajdah, Ṣād, and one of the Ḥawāmīm; none was in al-Mufaṣṣal."}, {"id": "7:206/q21/p6", "position": "Ten, omitting second al-Ḥajj, Ṣād, and three in al-Mufaṣṣal.", "reasons": "Attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās. Ibn ʿAbbās lists the ten sites as al-Aʿrāf, al-Raʿd, al-Naḥl, Banī Isrāʾīl, Maryam, one in al-Ḥajj, al-Naml, al-Furqān, al-Sajdah, and Ḥā Mīm al-Sajdah, with none in al-Mufaṣṣal. ʿAṭāʾ reports a ten-site list from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbbās naming the first al-Ḥajj prostration and the same other sūras."}, {"id": "7:206/q21/p7", "position": "Four: al-Sajdah, Fussilat, al-Najm, and al-ʿAlaq.", "reasons": "Reported by al-Qurṭubī and Abū Ḥayyān."}, {"id": "7:206/q21/p8", "position": "Twelve.", "reasons": "Al-Kāshifī as reported by Bursevī; he notes al-Shāfiʿī and Aḥmad accept the last al-Ḥajj sajdah while Abū Ḥanīfa excludes it, and schools differ on Ṣād because its wording mentions bowing though the Prophet prostrated."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q22", "question": "At which words in Fussilat is its recitation prostration?", "turns_on": "Whether precaution favors the later phrase or the report locating it at the earlier phrase.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q22/p1", "position": "At 41:38, lā yasʾamūn.", "reasons": "Bursevī follows ʿUmar and Ibn Masʿūd as precaution: delaying is allowed while doing it too early is not."}, {"id": "7:206/q22/p2", "position": "At 41:37, in kuntum iyyāhu taʿbudūn.", "reasons": "Bursevī reports this from ʿAlī and says al-Shāfiʿī follows it."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q23", "question": "Is recitation prostration obligatory?", "turns_on": "Whether the command, Satan report, and prophetic practice imply obligation or recommendation; al-Qurṭubī relies on ʿUmar's public statement.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q23/p1", "position": "No, it is a confirmed sunnah or recommended.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabrisī names al-Shāfiʿī and his companions; al-Qurṭubī cites Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and ʿUmar's public statement before Companions without objection, which he treats as consensus. He says the Satan report concerns an obligatory prostration elsewhere and prophetic practice indicates recommendation. The majority and Study Quran agree."}, {"id": "7:206/q23/p2", "position": "Yes, it is immediately obligatory on reciter and listener and made up if missed.", "reasons": "Abū Ḥanīfa cites the unqualified command, Satan's grief at Adam's child's obedience and reward, and the Prophet's practice; Bursevī states its immediate and make-up consequences."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q24", "question": "Who is required or invited to prostrate when the verse is heard?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q24/p1", "position": "The reciter and attentive listener prostrate; an incidental hearer is not obligated.", "reasons": "Ibn Kathīr says there is consensus for reciter and listener; Abū Ḥanīfa requires it for one who intended to listen; ʿUthmān limits it to attentive listening. ʿImrān's answer implies no duty for an unprepared hearer; Salmān and al-Sāʾib declined in relevant settings. Ibn ʿAmr reports that when the Prophet recited a sūra containing a prostration, he prostrated and the Companions followed, sometimes so crowded that they could find no room for their foreheads."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q25", "question": "What conditions apply to recitation prostration?", "turns_on": "Whether recitation prostration takes the purity conditions of prayer.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q25/p1", "position": "Prayer-like conditions apply: purity, intention, qibla, and permissible time.", "reasons": "Al-Qurṭubī lists the conditions; Abū Ḥayyān adds freedom from impurity and ritual defilement. Al-Zuhrī requires purity and qibla at home but allows a mounted traveler any direction."}, {"id": "7:206/q25/p2", "position": "Purity is not required.", "reasons": "Al-Bukhārī reports Ibn ʿUmar prostrating without purity; Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn al-Munkadir report al-Shaʿbī likewise."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q26", "question": "What takbīr and hand raising accompany the prostration?", "turns_on": "Whether rules inside prayer carry over outside it, especially hand raising and takbīr.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q26/p1", "po

sition": "Say takbīr and raise the hands for it.", "reasons": "Al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, and Isḥāq are cited by al-Qurṭubī and Abū Ḥayyān; Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet saying takbīr on descent and ascent."}, {"id": "7:206/q26/p2", "position": "Say takbīr on descent and ascent within prayer; hand raising applies within prayer, with differing reports outside.", "reasons": "Mālik's well-known position; al-Qurṭubī adds most jurists require takbīr outside prayer, and Abū Ḥayyān notes the varying reports."}, {"id": "7:206/q26/p3", "position": "For a seated worshipper, stand with takbīr, prostrate with takbīr, then sit.", "reasons": "Bursevī says this is fuller and unnecessary delay is disliked."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q27", "question": "Does recitation prostration end with salām?", "turns_on": "Whether analogy to prayer requires an exit salām; the two compilers give opposite majority attributions.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q27/p1", "position": "No salām is required.", "reasons": "Al-Qurṭubī reports this as majority practice; Abū Ḥayyān instead attributes no salām to a group of early authorities and Isḥāq."}, {"id": "7:206/q27/p2", "position": "Salām is required.", "reasons": "Ibn al-ʿArabī favors it because an act entered with takbīr needs an exit as prayer does, more so than funeral prayer. Al-Qurṭubī attributes this to early authorities and Isḥāq, while Abū Ḥayyān calls it the majority view."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q28", "question": "At what times may recitation prostration be performed?", "turns_on": "How a cause-specific sajdah interacts with bans on prayer after dawn and ʿAṣr, and why those bans apply.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q28/p1", "position": "At any time, as prayer with a specific cause.", "reasons": "Al-Shāfiʿī and others are reported by al-Qurṭubī and Abū Ḥayyān."}, {"id": "7:206/q28/p2", "position": "Until dawn brightens or until the sun yellows after ʿAṣr.", "reasons": "One Mālikī view reported by al-Qurṭubī."}, {"id": "7:206/q28/p3", "position": "Not after dawn and not after ʿAṣr.", "reasons": "One Mālikī view reported by al-Qurṭubī; Abū Ḥayyān also reports bans after dawn and afternoon prayers."}, {"id": "7:206/q28/p4", "position": "Allowed after dawn but not after ʿAṣr.", "reasons": "Another Mālikī view in al-Qurṭubī."}, {"id": "7:206/q28/p5", "position": "Not after sunrise until the sun is high.", "reasons": "Abū Ḥayyān reports this among Mālikī views."}, {"id": "7:206/q28/p6", "position": "Not after dawn only.", "reasons": "Abū Ḥayyān reports this among Mālikī views; al-Qurṭubī says these debates turn on the general prayer ban and its rationale."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q29", "question": "May one perform it during an obligatory prayer?", "turns_on": "Whether an extra sajdah is intrinsically excluded or only avoided to prevent congregational confusion.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q29/p1", "position": "No, in any obligatory prayer, whether alone or together and whether recited quietly or aloud.", "reasons": "Mālik's well-known ruling regards it as an added prostration."}, {"id": "7:206/q29/p2", "position": "Yes where the congregation will not be confused, especially when alone.", "reasons": "Another rationale in al-Qurṭubī is avoiding confusion. The Abū Rāfiʿ report describes Abū Hurayra prostrating during ʿIshāʾ at al-Inshiqāq, citing the Prophet's practice."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q30", "question": "May it be performed in voluntary congregational prayer when it could confuse worshippers?", "turns_on": "How much weight to give possible disruption in voluntary group prayer.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q30/p1", "position": "Yes, even if confusion is feared; certainly when it is not feared.", "reasons": "Al-Qurṭubī states this as the ruling, including solitary voluntary prayer."}, {"id": "7:206/q30/p2", "position": "No when it may confuse the congregation.", "reasons": "Al-Qurṭubī reports this alternative."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q31", "question": "What should be said during recitation prostration?", "turns_on": "Which transmitted supplication or glorification is used.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q31/p1", "position": "Recite glorification, especially subḥāna rabbī al-aʿlā three times.", "reasons": "Bursevī prefers this and also gives alternatives asking the Merciful for forgiveness or the Turner of hearts for steadfastness; al-Asrār al-Muḥammadiyya favors the latter. His cited Persian scholar gives site-specific requests at al-Isrāʾ, al-Aʿrāf or al-Sajdah, and al-Najm."}, {"id": "7:206/q31/p2", "position": "Use the Prophet's supplication about one's face prostrating to its Creator, with requests for reward and pardon.", "reasons": "Bursevī reports creation, hearing, sight, provision, and acceptance; ʿĀʾisha reports repeated use at night, graded authentic by al-Tirmidhī."}, {"id": "7:206/q31/p3", "position": "Ask God to lift burden, record reward, and store the sajdah as treasure.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās transmits this Prophetic supplication in al-Qurṭubī."}, {"id": "7:206/q31/p4", "position": "Ask for useful knowledge and deeds that raise one's rank.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿUmar's Prophetic report in al-Ālūsī."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q32", "question": "What merit or warning is reported for prostrating?", "turns_on": "Which Prophetic report is being cited.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q32/p1", "position": "Satan withdraws weeping when a human prostrates: the human obeys and gains Paradise, while he refused and faces Fire.", "reasons": "Reported from Abū Hurayra and in multiple commentaries; al-Qurṭubī says its commanded prostration concerns an obligation, while the Prophet's regular practice supports recommendation here."}, {"id": "7:206/q32/p2", "position": "Each prostration raises a degree and removes a sin, or grants both.", "reasons": "Al-Baghawī reports Thawbān from the Prophet; al-Ālūsī reports ʿĀʾisha."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q33", "question": "What virtue is reported for reciting Sūrat al-Aʿrāf?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q33/p1", "position": "It brings a screen from Iblīs on Judgment Day and Adam's intercession.", "reasons": "Al-Kashshāf and al-Bayḍāwī report this from the Prophet."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q34", "question": "What spiritual counsel is drawn from prostration here?", "turns_on": "Whether counsel focuses on chosen human prostration or universal submission.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q34/p1", "position": "Prostration is the proper response to divine command and a source of human honor.", "reasons": "Bursevī's Persian verses shame refusal, the Shaykh al-Islām's maxim censures a head absent from prostration, and another couplet couples generosity with nobility and prostration with honor."}, {"id": "7:206/q34/p2", "position": "All beings already submit to God's power before and during existence.", "reasons": "Bursevī says pre-eternal nonexistence bowed to God's power to create; existing beings surrender to His decrees of annihilation, creation, and preservation."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q35", "question": "What theological limits are set on inward readings?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q35/p1", "position": "God remains transcendent; talk of annihilation cannot imply indwelling, union, fusion, or identity of God and servant.", "reasons": "Bursevī explicitly rejects these claims and says God remains as in eternity."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q36", "question": "Is quiet remembrance preferable?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q36/p1", "position": "Yes, quiet remembrance is best.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī draws the inference and cites Aḥmad's report, 'The best remembrance is silent.' He also condemns contemporary ignorant Sufis' religiously and rationally objectionable practices."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q37", "question": "How does this sūra's ending suit its theme?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q37/p1", "position": "It closes by urging worship through the angels' example.", "reasons": "Al-Itqān compares distinctive endings of al-Māʾida, al-Anʿām, al-Anfāl, al-Tawba, Yūnus, Hūd, Yūsuf, and al-Raʿd; Kuran Yolu says the close calls for praise by heart and tongue, humble prostration, and preferring God's pleasure to desire."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q38", "question": "How are al-Anfāl and Barāʾa arranged after al-Aʿrāf?", "turns_on": "Length, thematic and opening links, codex order, and whether arrangement was fixed by revelation.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q38/p1", "position": "They form or function as a pair among the seven long sūras.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī reports early authorities treating the two as one and al-Naḥḥās's report from ʿUthmān that they were called twin sūras in the Prophet's time. An alternative would move Yūnus and Hūd as in Ubayy's codex."}, {"id": "7:206/q38/p5", "position": "Other codex ordering can follow descending sūra length and local thematic links.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī says Ibn Masʿūd placed al-Anfāl after al-Nūr, whose promise of inheriting l

{"id": "7:206/q39", "question": "What background reports about the sūra are appended here?", "turns_on": "These are separate appended reports on historical setting, commentary completion, and future communal trouble.", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q39/p1", "position": "Al-Aʿrāf is classed as late Meccan and reportedly followed Ṣād and preceded al-Anʿām.", "reasons": "Study Quran's introduction also summarizes its warning about rejecting signs and messengers through earlier prophetic stories and their consequences."}, {"id": "7:206/q39/p2", "position": "Bursevī completed the commentary in early Ṣafar 1101 AH before proceeding to al-Anfāl.", "reasons": "His colophon records the first ten days of the month."}, {"id": "7:206/q39/p3", "position": "Gabriel warned the Prophet of later discord, unjust rulers, and misguided reciters, with restraint and patience as protection.", "reasons": "Ṭabāṭabāʾī transmits ʿUmar's report about the Prophet."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q40", "question": "How does Ibn Kathīr urge believers to emulate the angels?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q40/p1", "position": "Imitate their abundant, constant worship and orderly prayer rows.", "reasons": "Ibn Kathīr says their unceasing glorification and prostration invite devotion; he cites a hadith urging Muslims to fill first rows and stand close together as angels do."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q41", "question": "Why do counts of Qurʾanic prostration sites differ?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q41/p1", "position": "Reports and practice vary, as does interpretation of prostration commands.", "reasons": "Al-Qurṭubī says some read commands as recitation prostration and others as required prayer prostration."}]}
{"id": "7:206/q42", "question": "Why do rulings on permitted times differ?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "7:206/q42/p1", "position": "Scholars weigh the recitation sajdah against general bans on prayer after dawn and ʿAṣr and differ over those bans' rationale.", "reasons": "Al-Qurṭubī's explanation."}]}
{"id": "8:38/q01", "question": "Who are the unbelievers addressed?", "turns_on": "Whether the reported occasion limits the address.", "positions": [{"id": "8:38/q01/p1", "position": "Abu Sufyan and his companions.", "reasons": "Al-Kalbi, Ibn Abbas via Abu Salih, al-Baydawi, al-Nasafi and al-Alusi identify this group; al-Wahidi al-Wajiz adopts it."}, {"id": "8:38/q01/p2", "position": "Disbelievers generally, including those beyond the immediate occasion.", "reasons": "Jishumi reports a general address beside the Abu Sufyan report; Ibn Ashur extends the rule to every disbeliever."}]}
{"id": "8:38/q02", "question": "What is the force of 'say to' and the third-person wording?", "turns_on": "Whether the lam marks transmission or benefit, and whether the condition quotes the address directly.", "positions": [{"id": "8:38/q02/p1", "position": "The lam conveys a message; the Prophet tells them its meaning in these or other words.", "reasons": "Ibn Atiyya, al-Qurtubi, Abu Hayyan and al-Samin allow paraphrase. Sahib al-Nazm says third person suits reporting speech to absent people, whereas direct quotation would use second person as in 3:12. Ibn Ashur says the Prophet reports the sense as an informed witness."}, {"id": "8:38/q02/p2", "position": "The lam is causal: the Prophet says this for their benefit, rather than directly addressing them in this wording.", "reasons": "Al-Zamakhshari argues direct speech would say 'if you desist, you will be forgiven'; Ibn Masud's wording illustrates it. Al-Samin cites 46:11. Al-Baydawi says 'say for their sake'."}, {"id": "8:38/q02/p3", "position": "Third-person reference expresses turning away from unbelievers while believers receive direct address.", "reasons": "Al-Burhan contrasts this wording with the command to believers in 8:39."}]}
{"id": "8:38/q03", "question": "What alternative readings of the promise are reported?", "turns_on": "Whether speaker and addressees appear explicitly in the verb forms.", "positions": [{"id": "8:38/q03/p1", "position": "Ibn Masud's wording addresses them directly: 'if you desist, you will be forgiven.'", "reasons": "Al-Kisai reports Ibn Masud's codex; Ibn Atiyya says that wording would require verbatim delivery, and al-Alusi says its lam must convey speech. Razi also cites the direct address."}, {"id": "8:38/q03/p2", "position": "The forgiveness verb is read actively, with God as its subject.", "reasons": "Al-Baydawi, Abu Hayyan and al-Samin report this reading."}, {"id": "8:38/q03/p3", "position": "A passive reading is reported with the pronoun referred to God.", "reasons": "Al-Alusi reports this formulation."}]}
{"id": "8:38/q04", "question": "What does 'desist' mean lexically?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "8:38/q04/p1", "position": "To stop an act because it has been prohibited.", "reasons": "Jishumi, al-Tabrisi and Tabatabai derive the sense from someone forbidding an act and another ceasing it."}]}
{"id": "8:38/q05", "question": "What must the unbelievers stop doing?", "turns_on": "Whether the condition requires conversion, peace, or both.", "positions": [{"id": "8:38/q05/p1", "position": "Abandon disbelief or idolatry and enter faith, with repentance.", "reasons": "Ibn Abbas specifies denial of Muhammad and association of partners; Ibn Atiyya reasons forgiveness of the past requires leaving disbelief. Jishumi stresses present idolatry. Others include accepting Islam and its law. Jishumi says fighting is obligatory only during persistent unbelief and forbidden after desistance."}, {"id": "8:38/q05/p2", "position": "Stop fighting or hostility, make peace, and resolve grievances.", "reasons": "Al-Kalbi specifies fighting Muhammad and companions; al-Mawardi and al-Tabrisi connect peace with removal of earlier liability. Study Quran notes that the wording itself does not demand conversion and cites 2:192–193."}, {"id": "8:38/q05/p3", "position": "Stop both unbelief and hostility or warfare against the Messenger.", "reasons": "Al-Asamm combines idolatry and fighting; Razi adds embracing Islamic law. Ibn Ashur highlights spending to obstruct God's path; Nasafi and Baydawi describe ending opposition by entering Islam."}]}
{"id": "8:38/q06", "question": "How is the promise of forgiveness expressed, and why?", "turns_on": "Whether the wording highlights the resulting pardon or implies a fuller causal statement.", "positions": [{"id": "8:38/q06/p1", "position": "The passive centers the benefit: past sins are erased in substance and trace, without punishment or reproach.", "reasons": "Al-Biqai explains the passive wording and the completeness of the erasure."}, {"id": "8:38/q06/p2", "position": "An omitted clause can explain that God forgives because He is forgiving and merciful.", "reasons": "Jishumi reports this supplied wording after repentance."}]}
{"id": "8:38/q07", "question": "What does 'what has passed' mean lexically?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "8:38/q07/p1", "position": "What has gone before or preceded.", "reasons": "Al-Wahidi relates salafa to advance payment, the forward neck and the first extracted wine; Jishumi notes salafa and aslafa; Tabatabai gives the basic sense. Tabrisi says salaf are those before."}]}
{"id": "8:38/q08", "question": "Which past acts are covered by the promise?", "turns_on": "Which conduct the first condition ends and what sort of pardon follows.", "positions": [{"id": "8:38/q08/p1", "position": "Prior unbelief and sins, including hostile acts, are erased on faith and repentance.", "reasons": "Ibn Abbas lists fornication, idolatry, murder, usury and every disapproved act; Jishumi includes fighting and persecution with no worldly retaliation or afterlife punishment. Ibn Ashur emphasizes removal of afterlife punishment; Nasafi singles out past hostility. Kuranyolu likens conversion to a clean page."}, {"id": "8:38/q08/p2", "position": "Past fighting and associated punishment or liability are forgiven when hostilities cease.", "reasons": "Al-Mawardi, al-Tabrisi and Ibn al-Jawzi state the peace reading; Study Quran allows ending hostilities and settling grievances without an explicit conversion requirement."}]}
{"id": "8:38/q09", "question": "What legal claims from before conversion survive?", "turns_on": "How the general promise interacts with divine duties, human claims, protected status and specific penalties.", "positions": [{"id": "8:38/q09/p1", "position": "A combatant convert's prior wrongs and missed worship are cleared broadly.", "reasons": "Malik is reported to waive accountability, including property and blood; scholars cite the hadith that Islam erases what preceded it, so no bodily or financial worship is made up. Ibn al-Arabi prefers broad pardon from the verse's general wording, the hadith and the incentive to convert. Al-Shafi'i's Iraq view waives preconversion adultery penalty; the Kufan authority agrees.
